newsitem.title: USA: Oakland police unravel bizarre murder tale.
newsitem.headline: Oakland police unravel bizarre murder tale.

text.p: In a plot worthy of Alfred Hitchcock, a woman hailed as a courageous fighter of drug dealers may have been murdered by her sister, who allegedly stashed the body in a freezer and then impersonated her, police said on Wednesday.

But the bizarre plot unravelled when the home of 52-year-old anti-drug crusader Stevie Allman was fire-bombed, supposedly by drug dealers, on July 1 and a woman claiming to be her was admitted to hospital suffering burns.
In an outpouring of support for the woman who videotaped transactions by drug dealers and gave the evidence to police, Californians sent money and Gov. Pete Wilson offered a $50,000 reward.

But Oakland police said on Wednesday they found out this week that the woman was in fact Allman's younger sister, Sarah, 47, who was masquerading as Stevie Allman. The two sisters had lived together and looked alike.
"This is the stuff of a Hollywood movie," Oakland police Capt. Peter Dunbar said.
Police searched the burned-out house on Tuesday, finding a decomposed body in a freezer. On Wednesday, the coroner's office positively identified the victim as Stevie Allman, Dunbar said.

"She died as a result of blunt trauma to the head," Dunbar, who is leading the investigation, said. The body was dismembered. The coroner had not been able to determine when she died, he said. The last time police had been able to verify that Stevie Allman was alive was in April.

Sarah Allman was arrested on Tuesday for investigation of murder and forgery. She allegedly cashed a cheque for several thousand dollars donated to Stevie Allman by well-wishers after the fire. She was due to be formally charged in court on Thursday.

"The motive may be financial gain by Sarah Allman," Dunbar said. He said police believed the house fire could have been started by drug dealers or could have been intended to hide evidence of the murder.
Sarah Allman, posing as her sister Stevie, basked in public support as she was treated at a local hospital for burns after the house fire.
A fund was set up for donations for Allman and a local contractor offered to rebuild the razed house at no charge.
After the woman got out of hospital, Oakland police received a tipoff that she was not Stevie Allman.
Police took the woman's fingerprints and confirmed that she was Sarah Allman. Under questioning, the woman finally admitted her true identity, police said.
